issues.legal_issue: Service of a written notice under Section 10(5) of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act is mandatory before possession may be taken under Section 10(6).
Possession under Section 10(6) cannot be taken until thirty days have elapsed from service of the Section 10(5) notice.
Section 10(6) does not require a separate notice or order after the period for compliance with a Section 10(5) notice has expired.
For the savings under the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Act, possession means actual physical possession, not merely deemed vesting or paper possession.
The State bears the burden of establishing by cogent evidence that possession was validly taken before the Repeal Act came into force.
A panchnama may evidence possession of a large tract of land, but its validity and the fact of possession remain subject to judicial scrutiny.
A writ court may determine whether actual possession was taken when that issue is necessary to decide the case and the record permits a finding, notwithstanding a dispute of fact.
An intra-court appellate bench should interfere with a single judge’s decision only where it contains a patent error or conflicts with settled legal principles.
A landholder’s failure to challenge non-compliance with Section 10(5) may amount to waiver only where the circumstances, including delay after dispossession, justify that conclusion.
